macro_context.market_sentiment: Markets are cautiously recovering on May 5, 2026 after Monday's sell-off: S&P 500 +0.78%, Nasdaq +0.90%, Russell 2000 +1.41% as Middle East tensions eased slightly and strong earnings from Palantir and others lifted sentiment. Oil remains elevated (WTI ~$104/bbl) but pulled back from Monday highs.
macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC voted 8-4 on April 29, 2026 to hold rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% — third consecutive hold. Inflation remains elevated partly due to global energy prices. Markets pricing zero rate changes through 2026, with one 25 bps cut not expected until December 2027.
macro_context.geopolitical: Escalating U.S.-Iran conflict (UAE intercepting Iranian missiles) drove oil sharply higher and hit cyclicals on May 4, 2026 before partial stabilization. Additional concerns include tariff uncertainty, U.S. midterm elections, and NATO/Greenland tensions. Middle East conflict is the dominant near-term market risk.

web_context.competitor_activity: Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and JNJ all delivered Q1 2026 business updates concurrently. Pharma peers Pfizer, Novartis, AstraZeneca, and Eli Lilly compete intensely on R&D and drug launches; medtech rivals Medtronic, Abbott, and Boston Scientific compete on device innovation. JNJ partnered with Lexeo Therapeutics for cardiac gene therapy delivery, opening a new competitive niche. Rising energy costs and Middle East uncertainty weigh on the broader sector, though defensives like pharma have seen relative inflows.
